text:
Second trip to Osaka? Stay where Osaka actually lives. 🏮

Namba and Umeda are the easy picks, and for a first trip we still suggest them.

But if you want to buy dinner where locals buy it, drink where office workers drink, and wake up to a quiet street, these are the two neighbourhoods we'd book.

━━━━━━━━━━
📍 1. TENMA
━━━━━━━━━━

Where: around JR Tenma Station and Ogimachi, just north of the city centre.

Why we like it:
• Japan's longest covered shopping street runs straight through it. Tenjinbashisuji is 2.6 km long with about 600 shops: croquettes, fish, pickles and old coffee shops.
• The back alleys just north of JR Tenma, known as Ura-Tenma, are packed with tiny izakaya under hundreds of lanterns. About 5 minutes on foot.
• It's lively at night, but local-lively: office workers and neighbours, not tour groups.

Getting around:
🚃 1 stop to Osaka Station on the JR Loop Line, for Kyoto trains, the airport express and Universal Studios connections
🚇 About 10 minutes south to Nipponbashi on the Sakaisuji Line

━━━━━━━━━━
📍 2. TSURUHASHI
━━━━━━━━━━

Where: Osaka's Korean neighbourhood, on the east side of the Loop Line.

Why we like it:
• It's famous for yakiniku, and the market lanes start right outside the station.
• Miyuki-dori Koreatown is a 10–15 minute walk south.
• Three lines meet here: JR Loop Line, Kintetsu and the Sennichimae Line.

Getting around:
🚇 Sennichimae Line direct to Namba, no change needed
🦌 Kintetsu Nara Line trains stop here, so it's a smart base if Nara is on your list

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ OUR TAKE
━━━━━━━━━━

Go local if it's your second trip, you love food, you want quieter mornings, or you're staying four nights or more.

Stay central if it's your first trip and you only have two or three nights. It simply saves time.

Full guide with lines, walking times and hotels 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-live-like-a-local
